column1: # THE DESCENT SPINES DRAWN ON /uruguay/ - THREE HOUSES, ONE FILE.
# *** WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, and it is one day old. *** These three ladders were HAND-WRITTEN
# in site/src/pages/uruguay.astro, and hand-written descent went stale TWICE IN TWO DAYS:
#   22 Sep - gen 4 of the Sancho house said "Alejandro Maximo (1839-1903)", asserting an
#            identification data/the-three-alejandros.tsv has never been able to make, on a
#            year two Montevideo acts put five years out.
#   22 Sep - gen 3 said Avelino died "23 August 1890, La Paz, Canelones". He died on the
#            *** 22nd, at Montevideo, and was REGISTERED the next day ***. Both the wrong date
#            and the wrong place came from data/montevideo-lerena-trunk.tsv, a file whose own
#            header says "TIER: SECONDARY THROUGHOUT ... no row here may be cited as fact".
# The same row also said Avelino was "the seventh of eight children". He is the EIGHTH of eight,
# or the seventh of seven if Fidel - the only one attested at second hand - is set aside. There
# is no count under which the published phrase was right.
# *** THE POINT IS NOT THAT SOMEBODY MISTYPED. *** tools/check-inline.py had been reporting
# these ladders for days - "reachable only by editing the page" - and nothing gated them, so a
# tree value could be published as fact and no check would ever see it. A spine in a TSV is a
# spine tools/drift.py and the emphasis and raggedness checks can reach.
# weak = "yes" marks THE JOINT THAT CANNOT BEAR WEIGHT, and weakNote says why.
# note and weakNote hold HTML deliberately: these cells are rendered with set:html.

column11: Named on their son's marriage act of 1791 and again on a grandson's baptism of 1811, where the father is written Feliz Gerena. Not yet found in any Spanish register.

column1: sancho
column12: Married at Canelones, 8 January 1791. A dragoon; in 1798 he swore an oath and could not sign his name. She natural de las Asturias, daughter of Rodrigo and Rosa Fernández.

column1: sancho
column12: The youngest of Sancho’s children, born between 1793 and 1815 — eight of them counting Fidel, who is attested only at second hand. Father of the Lerena Traibel. His death was registered the next day, which is where the family tree’s “23 August, La Paz, Canelones” comes from; this page carried that until 22 September 2026. See corrections.

column1: sancho
column12: Alejandro — baptised at La Mauricia 7 January 1846, the eldest known, and whether he is the Alejandro Máximo of the Argentine cards is open — Carlos Ambrosio (1842–1893, who married his cousin Luisa Lerena Lenguas), Alberto (1852–1921) — whose death is Montevideo certificate 246 — and eight more. The other branch, the Lerena Lenguas, runs beside them.

column1: ramon
column11: Named as the paternal grandparents on the act of 15 November 1812. Not yet found in any Spanish register — but their son's birthplace is now known, which makes them findable.
column12: The tree’s otherwise unexplained “Ramón Llerena Cubas” is her surname.

column1: ramon
column12: So the act of 1812 writes him; the indexes say Lerena and Gerena. She natural de la Ysla de Canarias, Lanzarote, daughter of Marcial de León González and Ysavel Lorenza. Fathering children from about 1800.

column1: ramon
column12: Alejandro, born Rosario, married Margarita Fernández Álvarez at San José, 16 September 1825. Mauricio, born Colla, married Casimira Montaño at San José de Mayo, 3 February 1837. Their brothers Manuel Lorenzo (1812) and Luís Manuel (1820).

column1: ramon
column12: Two of the six or seven Trinidad fathers, and first cousins: Bernabé is Alejandro’s son, Cipriano is Mauricio’s. With Vitalino, Ysaac, Fermín and Florencio they fathered the Flores kindred, marrying Basque women — Beloqui, Echeverry, Pelaez — until the church required a dispensation for consanguinity.

column11: Named by their son on his Argentine enrolment card, filled in at the consulate in Cape Town. There is no other record of either of them anywhere on earth — not a baptism, not a marriage, not a burial, in Argentina or Uruguay.
column12: Her surname is written as his; whether she was a Lerena by birth is not known.

column12: In South Africa Robert Paul Lerena. Racehorse trainer. Married at Wynberg in 1911; three generations on to David’s mother, with no inferred link in the descent.
